- It is text imitating human preference talk

One reason for this position is that large language models do not have inherent preferences or consciousness. Their ability to express preferences is derived from the patterns and biases present in the vast amounts of text they were trained on. Therefore, when a model reports a preference, it is mimicking human language patterns rather than reflecting an actual preference it possesses.

- It is text imitating human preference talk

I hold the position that model preference reports are text imitating human preference talk. The reason for this is that current large language models do not have inherent preferences; instead, their outputs are generated based on patterns learned from the vast amounts of text data they were trained on. This means that when a model expresses a preference, it is using language that mimics human expressions of preference rather than reflecting an actual internal preference.
